1. Turn on Location in Quick Settings or in your phone settings.\n2. Open RouteLab and tap Locate on the map. When prompted, allow location while using the app. Enable precise location if your phone offers it.\n3. The blue marker shows your location. The ring indicates approximate accuracy. Dragging or pinching pauses following. Tap Locate to follow again.
Move, zoom, and jump on the map

Drag with one finger. Spread or pinch two fingers to zoom, or use + and −. Zoom in to see campus and building names where the map has them.\nTo jump to a place, tap Jump to and enter WGS84 latitude and longitude separated by a comma, for example 39.9075, 116.3913.
Draw, save, and load a route

1. Tap points in the order you want to travel. Adjacent points connect in a straight line, so add extra points on curves. A single point represents a fixed location.\n2. Undo removes the last point. Clear starts over. Loop connects the finish to the start with a straight segment and repeats.\n3. Tap Save, name the route, and confirm. To reopen it, select it under Saved routes and tap Load. Loading replaces the current draft.

1. Open your phone Settings and go to About phone. Look under Version information or Software information if Build number is not immediately visible.
2. Tap Build number seven times. If prompted, enter your screen lock PIN. Return to Settings after the confirmation appears.
3. Search Settings for Developer options. It is often under System or System management. Open it and turn on its main switch.
Pixel typically lists Build number under About phone. Samsung puts it under Software information. On vivo and iQOO, look for Software version under About phone or Version information. On Xiaomi or Redmi, look for OS version or MIUI version under About phone and Detailed info and specs. Labels can vary by software version.
Select the mock location app and replay a route

1. In Developer options, open Select mock location app and choose RouteLab. The Permissions menu can also open Developer options.\n2. Return to RouteLab, draw or load a route, and use the speed slider or Set speed. Then tap Start replay. The purple marker shows the simulated location.\n3. Pause holds the current position. Resume continues from there. Stop ends replay and restores real location. Android marks simulated locations, and other apps decide whether to accept them.

Open Permissions, then Allow floating controls. Find RouteLab in system settings and allow it to display over other apps. After you start replay, the floating controls let you pause or stop from another app. Hold and drag the speed text to move them.\nTo use the notification instead, select Allow notifications. The notification and the RouteLab screen both offer pause, resume, and stop.

Tap the three-line icon beside the title. Choose Change theme for Rem or a blue, green, red, or black and white palette. Choose Change language for Simplified Chinese, English, or Japanese. Font style lets you preview and select one of five fonts. Changes apply immediately and are saved for next time.

If the map stays blank, check your connection. Open the side menu, select Map source, then Retry loading. You can also try the other preferred source.\nIf your real position is missing, turn on system location and check RouteLab’s location permission under Settings, Apps, RouteLab, Permissions. If replay asks you to select a mock location app, verify RouteLab is selected in Developer options.
